sources.name: Avalanche Metrics API
sources.authority: Ava Labs' official derived metrics behind the Avalanche explorer. Authoritative for the aggregates it defines; definitions are endpoint-specific and units are not documented, so each series is reconciled against raw-data datasets where one exists.
sources.authentication: none; the public endpoint answers keyless requests with a page limit of 2160 points, so each series is captured as fixed two-year windows
sources.reuse_status: Public access observed; Ava Labs terms apply to redistribution.
notes: OpenAPI /v2/networks/{network}/metrics/{metric}: Gets staking metrics for a given subnet. NetworkMetric enum: delegatorCount, delegatorWeight, validatorCount, validatorWeight.

OpenAPI /v2/chains/{chainId}/metrics/{metric}: EVM chain metrics are available for all Avalanche L1s on Mainnet and Fuji. All metrics are updated several times every hour. Each metric data point has a value and timestamp (Unix timestamp in seconds). All metric values include data within the duration of the associated timestamp plus the requested timeInterval. All timestamps are fixed to the hour.
OpenAPI MetricsValue.value: Aggregated value for the current metrics. MetricsValue.timestamp: Unix Epoch timestamp for which metrics are aggregated; for a day interval this is the start of the day.

Chain 43114 is the C-Chain. The API serves no P-Chain chain metrics (HTTP 404 for the Primary Network subnet ID), so P-Chain fees and burn come from the Snowflake P_TRANSACTIONS columns FEE and BURNED_AVAX instead.
Both series begin 2021-01-01; earlier dates are absent from the API although the Primary Network has staking history from 2020-09-10.

Reconciliation on 2026-09-19 against the end-of-day active set rebuilt from the Snowflake validator and delegator datasets: validator counts differ by a median 1.1 percent in 2021 to 2023, 2.1 percent in 2024, 2.8 percent in 2025, and 3.4 percent in 2026; delegator counts by 1.5 to 2.4 percent in 2021 to 2022 and 5.5 to 8 percent from 2023. Sampled days in 2022 and 2024 match exactly at end of day, so the residual reflects the API's undocumented aggregation instant plus an undercount from 2025 that also skips nine days between 2025-10-12 and 2025-12-01.

sources.name: Avalanche Data API
sources.authority: Ava Labs' official indexed data behind the Avalanche explorer. Its supply endpoint reports current totals, while its C-Chain Primary Network transaction endpoint reports atomic imports and exports with AVAX input and output amounts.
sources.authentication: optional; the OpenAPI security scheme is an x-glacier-api-key header. The supply and C atomic transaction endpoints answered keyless requests in September 2026. A key raises rate limits and is never stored in the repository.
sources.reuse_status: Public access observed; Ava Labs terms apply to redistribution.
notes: OpenAPI GET /v1/avax/supply: Get AVAX supply information that includes total supply, circulating supply, total p burned, total c burned, total x burned, total staked, total locked, total rewards, and last updated. The operation takes no parameters.

Blocker recorded 2026-09-19: the Data API exposes no historical supply, circulating supply, staked supply, or cumulative burn series; the supply endpoint returns one current state with lastUpdated. A history can only be assembled by repeated captures or from the Snowflake block supply counter.
Observed 2026-09-19: totalSupply equals genesisUnlock plus totalRewards minus the three burn totals to within one AVAX, so the API's totals are internally consistent.

C-Chain atomic transaction listing pages backward from latest; startTimestamp and endTimestamp require an address filter, so a complete all-address dated capture walks pages until it crosses the requested start.

observed_semantics: Delegation METADATA carries validator.weight as the delegated nAVAX and validator.nodeID as the target validator
Every delegation period observed on 2026-09-14 lies inside one validator staking period on the same node
The delegator identity is the address on the staked UTXOs; a small number of delegations are funded by several addresses

parameters.name: start
parameters.meaning: inclusive lower bound on the reward transaction timestamp, UTC

parameters.name: end
parameters.default: the UTC day after the capture date
parameters.meaning: exclusive upper bound on the reward transaction timestamp, UTC

observed_semantics: RewardValidatorTx.STAKING_TX_HASH is null on every row; METADATA txID names the staking transaction, exactly one reward per staking period
Reward UTXOs (REWARD = TRUE) carry the staking transaction hash, not the reward transaction hash
Rewarded validator periods receive at least the potential reward; the excess is delegation fee income
Rewarded delegator periods receive at most the potential reward; the shortfall is the validator's fee
Reward transactions land within one hour of the period end; a period with REWARDED = NULL has no reward transaction yet

observed_semantics: P_BLOCKS.CURRENT_SUPPLY is a JSON object keyed by subnet ID; the Primary Network value is the supply after the block, null only at height 0
Block heights are contiguous from 0, so the previous block is height minus one
The protocol supply counter rises by each new staker's potential reward and falls by the potential reward of a staker that ends unrewarded
Genesis validators carry BLOCK_HEIGHT -1 and have no block supply context

parameters.name: end
parameters.default: the UTC day after the capture date

observed_semantics: BURNED_AVAX holds the transaction's recorded AVAX destruction in nAVAX, despite its column name
Some P-Chain hashes repeat in the share; a row with a recorded burn takes precedence over null duplicates
AdvanceTimeTx and RewardValidatorTx with null BURNED_AVAX are zero-burn system transactions; another null burn remains missing and raises a check finding
FEE is not a substitute for BURNED_AVAX, especially before Etna

sources.name: Derived datasets
sources.authority: No external authority. A derived dataset is a deterministic transformation of built runs of other datasets in this catalog, and inherits their authority and limits. Its receipt records the exact input runs and their hashes.
sources.reuse_status: Follows the reuse status of its inputs.
notes: Built with `avalanche data derive`, which selects the newest built run of each input unless a run is pinned, and writes a capture receipt naming the input runs beside the Parquet build.
The staking-period log adds the network upgrade regime at acceptance and the reward the protocol kernel computes for each row, so the recorded potential reward can be checked row by row.

inputs.role: supply reading before each staking transaction's block

datasets.name: Primary Network validator staking transactions
studies: How Do Avalanche Validators Actually Think About Staking Rewards?
datasets.description: One row per accepted AddValidatorTx or AddPermissionlessValidatorTx on the Avalanche Primary Network with the chosen duration, delegation fee, stake weight, potential reward, and a staked-UTXO reconciliation.

fields.name: block_height
fields.unit: P-Chain block height; -1 for genesis validators

fields.name: rewarded
fields.unit: null while the staking period is in progress

fields.name: staked_utxo_count
fields.derivation: count of distinct UTXOS.UTXO_ID with STAKED = TRUE for the transaction

fields.name: utxo_stake_navax
fields.unit: nAVAX; null when no staked UTXO row exists
fields.derivation: sum of distinct UTXOS.AMOUNT with STAKED = TRUE for the transaction

datasets.name: Primary Network delegation transactions
studies: How Do Avalanche Validators Actually Think About Staking Rewards?
datasets.description: One row per accepted AddDelegatorTx or AddPermissionlessDelegatorTx on the Avalanche Primary Network with the target validator, the containing validator staking period, the funding address, duration, stake, potential reward, and a staked-UTXO reconciliation.

fields.name: validator_transaction_hash
fields.unit: P-Chain transaction ID; null when no validator period contains the delegation
fields.derivation: latest-starting validator staking transaction on the same node whose period contains the delegation period

fields.name: delegator_address
fields.unit: P-Chain address; null when no staked UTXO row exists
fields.derivation: address funding the largest share of distinct UTXOS.AMOUNT with STAKED = TRUE for the transaction

fields.name: delegator_address_count
fields.derivation: count of distinct UTXOS.ADDRESS on staked UTXOs for the transaction

fields.name: rewarded
fields.unit: null while the delegation period is in progress

fields.name: staked_utxo_count
fields.derivation: count of distinct UTXOS.UTXO_ID with STAKED = TRUE for the transaction

fields.name: utxo_stake_navax
fields.unit: nAVAX; null when no staked UTXO row exists
fields.derivation: sum of distinct UTXOS.AMOUNT with STAKED = TRUE for the transaction

datasets.name: Primary Network staking reward outcomes
studies: How Do Avalanche Validators Actually Think About Staking Rewards?
datasets.description: One row per reward transaction closing a validator or delegator staking period on the Avalanche Primary Network, with the linked staking period, its rewarded flag, potential reward, realized reward from reward UTXOs, and the resulting fee transfer.

fields.name: staking_tx_type
fields.unit: one of the four staking types; null when no Primary Network staking period matches

fields.name: realized_reward_navax

fields.name: fee_transfer_navax

fields.name: reward_utxo_count

datasets.name: Primary Network staking supply context
studies: How Do Avalanche Validators Actually Think About Staking Rewards?
datasets.description: One row per staking transaction on the Avalanche Primary Network with the AVAX supply before and after its block and the in-block supply deltas, the inputs the protocol reward formula used for the transaction's potential reward.

fields.name: tx_type
fields.unit: one of the four staking types

fields.name: block_height
fields.unit: P-Chain block height; -1 for genesis validators

fields.name: previous_block_supply_navax

fields.name: in_block_total_delta_navax
